record.title: Cambodia closes informal Thailand frontier routes during migrant-worker crackdown
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Informal land crossings on Cambodia–Thailand frontier; reported in Banteay Meanchey and Battambang, not every official international gate
record.crossings: Multiple informal routes; RFA names Tumnup Dach with unresolved locality description
record.direction: Documented outbound restrictions from Cambodia; full direction-by-route implementation not known.
record.movement: Informal-route users including daily workers and market traders; some outbound local trips explicitly barred.
record.exceptions: Returnees permitted; July4 instructions supported lawful worker passage. No universal official-gate prohibition inferred.
record.imposing_authority: Cambodian border authorities following Interior Ministry instruction
record.enforcement: Named Cambodian officials reported closures; national implementation not independently enumerated.
record.consequences: Reported difficulty for daily cross-border livelihoods; scale unmeasured.
record.relationship: Promotes narrowed R11-AS-L001; no merger with different2019security restrictions.
record.status_observation: Historical event only; no present-status inference.
record.official_rationale: Prevent irregular cross-border labour movement; officials also cited untaxed goods.
record.context: Actual suppression of informal crossing routes, not visa issuance alone. Reporting follows Thai enforcement of migrant employment rules.
record.uncertainty: July1andJuly3onsets differ across officials/outlets, possibly reflecting order versus implementation and nonidentical routes. Month precision retains conflict. RFA all-checkpoints wording is not adopted; its TumnupDach administrative location is unresolved. Endpoint and nationwide implementation unestablished.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible: onset contested and endpoint unknown.

No endpoint or route-complete implementation evidence.
